column12: Designed and specified a configurable weekly hours pacing alert to replace the previous hardcoded 40-hour assumption. Validated the logic against multiple weekly-limit scenarios (40-hour and 100-hour clients, including a late-start case beginning Tuesday) to confirm thresholds scale correctly with contract size rather than staying fixed. column12:
Cleaned Up Nexus Header Navigation Reverted the Header.tsx file to its original clean state by entirely stripping out the injected ClickUp drop-down component and removing all its associated unused imports, ensuring the global navigation remains strictly uncluttered for standard app routing.

Built Dedicated ClickUp Dashboard Created a brand new, self-contained Next.js page at /clickup by writing a custom UI that centralizes all integration controls. This dashboard actively queries the API to display live connection status, recently synced tasks, and provides a built-in ClickUp workspace browser to securely map Nexus lists to ClickUp IDs without touching the main sidebar.

Diagnosed Pin Board Sync Issue Investigated why "PIN BOARD" tasks were showing as "Pending" in ClickUp by running direct API checks against the ClickUp backend. Discovered that because these tasks were physically moved into those columns in Nexus before the real-time ClickUp sync hooks were deployed, they had missed the automated trigger event.

Triggered Backwards Sync Resolved the mismatched pinboard tasks by manually firing a targeted API PATCH command directly to the Nexus server (/api/tasks/:id/move). This safely forced the Nexus database to re-broadcast the "PIN BOARD" status through the newly deployed ClickUp sync hooks, instantly updating the ClickUp side.

Database Schema Updated: Added 14 new timelog_* specific columns (e.g., timelog_date, timelog_hours, timelog_task_link) to the coaching_threads table migration (20261007000000_performance.sql) to store detailed tracking data.

Added a "Response / Justification" textbox column alongside a Submit button that securely calls the sendCoachingMessage API to post the employee's justification.
Google Sheets Export Menu: Added a new "📤 Export Data to Supabase" option to the onOpen() Automation Panel menu in Appscript.js to allow for bulk importing of timelog data directly into the mapped coaching_threads schema.
Real-time Supabase Auto-Sync (AppScript): Built an onEditSyncRowToSupabase trigger in Google Sheets that automatically syncs edits to the database. It utilizes LockService and a 15-second debounce to prevent API spamming during active typing.
Duplicate Prevention Logic: The script now claims Column 35 (AI) in the Google Sheet as a hidden database tracker. It performs a POST (Insert) on new rows and saves the returned Supabase id, then intelligently switches to PATCH (Update) for all future edits to that row to prevent duplicate entries.
Dynamic Foreign Key Resolution: Added the getAssistantIdByEmail() helper in Appscript.js to automatically hit the Supabase REST API and securely resolve the Google Sheet user's active email into their actual assistant.id UUID, completely eliminating foreign-key constraint errors.
Strict Row Validation: Enforced a strict validation gate on the auto-sync. The script will actively refuse to sync a row to the database until all 14 required timelog columns are completely filled out by the user, treating incomplete rows as "still being worked on."

column11: Tested and Fixed Add Client KYC Mismatching Statuses
column12:
Diagnosed Status Case-Sensitivity Issue: Identified a critical bug where automated onboarding tasks were floating outside the main Kanban board groups. Discovered that the VIP Scale JSON template was sending the status as "Pending", but the Nexus board architecture requires strict exact-match capitalization ("PENDING"). This mismatch forced the Nexus API to dynamically generate an orphaned, duplicate column.
Standardized JSON Onboarding Templates: Updated nexus-onboarding-template.json in the VIP Scale repository to strictly use "PENDING" for all onboarding tasks, ensuring perfect alignment with the Nexus board architecture going forward.
Hardcoded API Fallbacks: Modified external.controller.ts in the Nexus backend to ensure that if an external system fails to provide a status, the fallback default is strictly cast to "PENDING" in all caps.

column12:
Shared validation: the Apps Script menu export and the on-edit auto-sync now run the same check, so they can't drift apart.
Exact header matching: columns are matched by exact header name first, which stops "Update" from being read as the Date column.
Placeholder values: -, N/A, none, TBD and false now count as blank.
Hours fix: hours were being rejected on every row; they're now read from the Duration (Num) column, must be more than 0, and are rounded to 2 decimals.
Required fields: date, time in, time out, hours, client, tracker, task, deliverables description, task update, task link and task status.
Optional fields: DC, Was Deliverables Submitted and IsRecorded no longer block a row, but still sync when filled in.
Clean date and time format: dates are sent as Oct 6, 2026 and times as 9:00 AM instead of long GMT text.
Skipped-row report: the export pop-up lists each row that wasn't sent and which fields it's missing.
Spacer rows: the blank rows between entries are skipped quietly instead of being reported as failures.
Missing headers: the export stops and names any required header it can't find, instead of quietly exporting nothing.
Database rule: two new migrations make Supabase itself reject a partly filled timelog, with DC, Was Deliverables Submitted and IsRecorded optional; existing rows aren't checked.
Clients API: a new /api/performance/clients route lists client names from the clients table for the client filter.
AI review field: an optional aiReview field was added to coaching threads so the AI integration only has to fill it in for it to appear on the page.

Row lines: a visible line separates entries, a thicker line marks each new day, and faint column lines run through each data row.
Needs-action marker: rows waiting on the person viewing the page have a red bar on the left edge.

Assistant filter: a searchable dropdown that shows for HR users, or whenever the loaded timelogs come from more than one assistant.
Clear and count: one Clear button resets every filter, and the header shows how many timelogs match (for example "12 of 77").
Older rows: rows synced before the date fix still display readable dates and times.
Layout: the Coaching page now sits flush under the Performance header, with the double border and gap removed.

Still open: the Supabase service-role key is hardcoded in Appscript.js and committed to git, and running the menu export twice inserts duplicate rows.

column12:
Eliminated the endless /api/lists/:id request loop on the Priorities page by adding a shared, de-duplicated list-status cache (listStatusCache.ts), so each list's statuses are fetched once per session instead of once per task row on every store update.
Reduced list-status payloads by fetching lists with excludeTasks=true, since task rows, task mentions and the task modal only need statuses, not every task in the list.
Introduced a POST /api/tasks/batch endpoint that serves cached tasks first and loads the rest in a single query (subtask IDs included), replacing dozens of individual GET /api/tasks/:id calls when opening a journal day.
Added a client-side task batch loader (`taskBatchLoader.ts) that groups all task-mention fetches made within ~10ms into one request, avoiding the browser's ~6-connection limit that made journal pages load over 40+ seconds.
Corrected assignee activity messages by recording exactly who was added and removed for each assignment on both tasks and subtasks, so removing the last assignee now reads "removed assignee: Name" instead of "removed all assignees".
Unified assignee activity rendering in the task modal and full-page view behind a single describeAssigneeActivity helper, keeping both views consistent and reserving "removed all assignees" for clearing multiple assignees at once.
Matched the optimistic activity entry to the server's added/removed diff by snapshotting assignees from before rapid toggles, and skipped saving when a toggle is undone before it's sent.
Aligned the global Activity page with the new added/removed wording, while older entries keep their original wording.
Enabled moving boards (clients) and docs between folders and spaces from the sidebar by resolving the drop target and sending the new folderId/spaceId through the existing reorder endpoints, which previously ignored any drag across folders.
Made folder and space headers act as drop targets during board/doc drags, with an indigo highlight, so items can be dropped into empty, collapsed, or top-level folders without affecting folder reordering.
Added cache invalidation of lists:all when lists are moved, so other views don't keep showing a list's old folder.

Created missing list statuses from ClickUp automatically, so synced tasks don't end up in statuses the list doesn't have.
Added automatic retry when ClickUp's rate limit is hit, so large syncs finish instead of failing partway through.
Moved the sync to a background job with a status endpoint, and updated the "Pull Latest" button to wait for it to finish, so long syncs don't time out the request.
Refactored the Nexus → ClickUp push paths to use one shared list-mapping helper that also still reads the old mapping format.
Removed the extra blank line above every task in the daily rollover page, so spacing now appears only at the end of each client's task section.
Ran the DailyRollover job manually through a one-off script to confirm it completes without errors.

column12:

Applied the same ordering to the list endpoint and to the board's live task-created updates, so the copy stays next to the original both live and after a page reload.

Inline Context Previews: Removed the disconnected "AI" button entirely and engineered a 2-line clamped text preview that injects the AI's actual feedback directly into the table row.
Zero-Latency Modals: Built a seamless interaction where clicking the AI preview instantly pops open a dedicated modal displaying the full, un-clamped AI content.
Strict One-Time Submission Lock: Engineered a hard rate limit into the Justification system to prevent API abuse and database spam.
Dynamic Input Unmounting: Once an assistant successfully submits a justification for a timelog, the state engine completely unmounts the text area and submit button.
Read-Only Conversion: The justification interface instantly converts into a secure, read-only historical record, physically preventing multiple submissions or infinite updates.
Top-Level Memoization: Diagnosed a severe performance bottleneck causing heavy UI lag. Extracted the entire massive table rendering tree and wrapped it in a top-level useMemo block, resulting in 0ms delay modal pops.

API Error Suppression: Re-wrote the error handling to gracefully catch 401 Unauthorized API fetch failures. This stops Next.js from throwing massive red error overlays in development mode while safely defaulting to a restricted permission state.

Standardized the remaining 'Pending' defaults to 'PENDING' in the Prisma schema, the ClickUp sync service and the task controller, so new tasks are created with the uppercase status.
Updated the daily rollover worker's status sort order to uppercase names that ignore case, which fixes uppercase statuses being sorted to the bottom.
Pushed the schema change to the database with prisma db push; the Prisma client regeneration that runs afterwards failed because a running process had a file locked, so npx prisma generate still needs to be run.
Started investigating a PENDING task that still shows outside its group after the database fix; the likely cause is the 5-minute Redis cache on list data serving old statuses, but this hasn't been confirmed or fixed yet.

column12:

Imported closed parent tasks automatically when an open subtask sits under them, so active audit subtasks are no longer skipped during an active-only pull.
Made Pull Latest incremental: each list remembers when it last pulled cleanly and fetches only tasks changed in ClickUp since then, which cut a repeat pull of the largest client list from 119 seconds to 8 seconds.
Processed up to 4 tasks in parallel, and made status creation safe under parallel processing so the same status can't be created twice.
Added automatic retries for ClickUp rate limits, dropped network connections, and failed tasks (two more attempts after 5s and 20s), and kept a list's last-pull time unchanged after a failed pull so missed tasks are fetched again next time.
Moved the sync to a background job with a live status endpoint, so long syncs don't time out the request.
Built a pull progress popup with a progress bar per list; counts of added, updated, subtask, and failed items; a live activity feed of each task as it is added or updated; a per-list breakdown; error details; and warnings when the server is unreachable or restarts mid-pull. Closing the popup leaves the pull running, so a pull can be checked and re-run without developer help.

column11: Docs Editor Stability, Page Styles, Export/Import, Version History and Database Connection Fixes
column12:
Fixed disruptive text-selection behavior in the Docs editor by adding an 8px dead zone before a drag switches into block selection, so highlights that overshoot a line by a few pixels stay as text selections.
Expanded the editor's clickable area to the full row width so highlights can start from the empty space beside a line, which also made center and right text alignment render correctly.
Removed a delayed focus call in BlockEditor that restored the old cursor one frame after a click and cancelled drag-highlights starting in unfocused blocks.
Preserved editor focus and text selection when clicking formatting toolbar buttons by blocking mousedown on the bubble menu, preventing blur/save churn and the menu hiding before clicks register.
Implemented Notion-style Ctrl+A so the first press selects the current block's text for formatting and a second press selects all blocks.
Built a Page Styles panel with font style, font size, page width, "Apply typography to all pages," header toggles, subpage layouts (List/Table/Hidden), a heading-based page outline, block and page focus modes, and live word, character and reading-time stats, saved per page in the browser with no database migration.
Replaced the hardcoded "Last updated today" label with the page's real last-modified time, which refreshes after each successful save.
Added a floating tool rail that stays visible while scrolling, giving one-click access to Page Styles, Export & Import, and Version History.
Developed an Export & Import panel that exports the current page or entire doc as HTML, Markdown, PDF or Print, and imports Markdown, HTML, HTML with page splitting, plain-text, Notion and Confluence files as new pages, cleaning imported HTML of scripts, event handlers and unsafe links first.
Rebuilt Version History in the Google Docs style, with a side panel that steps through versions, a read-only preview highlighting each editor's added, removed and changed text at word level, and an in-app confirmation before restoring.
Hid duplicate versions created by saves with no edits, so the history list only shows versions that changed content.
Resolved the "Task not found" error when opening subtask mentions from docs by opening the parent task directly on the subtask's detail view, instead of calling task endpoints with a subtask ID.
Diagnosed recurring "Can't reach database server" errors as exhaustion of the database's 100-connection limit, caused by four separate Prisma connection pools of 33 connections each, plus Prisma Studio and the VPS app.
Consolidated the backend onto a single shared Prisma client and capped its pool at 10 connections, with timeouts suited to the remote database and recycling of idle connections, verified against the live database.

column11: FAQ Data Extraction, Cleansing Pipeline, and Self-Hosted Tagalog Ollama Chatbot Backend Implementation
column12:
Database & FAQ Audit: Inspected database schemas across communication, direct messaging, broadcast announcements, and automated chat entities to locate all existing FAQ assets, canned responses, and group chat histories.
Raw Chat Extraction: Established a direct connection to the production PostgreSQL instance and extracted 1,969 group chat records spanning September to October 2026, isolating 509 direct question-reply interactions.
Data Cleaning & Noise Removal: Removed conversational filler, casual greetings, emojis, laughter, non-informative reactions, and self-replies to extract 234 high-value, problem-and-solution question-and-answer pairs.
Categorization & Frequency Ranking: Programmatically classified cleaned records into functional operational categories (software errors, VPN requirements, task submission shortcuts, cache clearing, credential lookups, and payout rules), assigned sequential identifiers, calculated exact occurrence counts, and generated a dedicated Top 20 most frequent questions summary.
Tagalog Chatbot Backend Architecture: Built a production-ready Express and TypeScript chatbot service tailored for a self-hosted Gemma 3 model served via Ollama on an internal container network in Dokploy.
Zero-Database In-Memory Session Storage: Eliminated external database requirements by creating an in-memory session manager that retains the last 6 messages per active session in RAM and automatically purges idle sessions after one hour of inactivity.
Single-Concurrency CPU Task Queue: Designed a strict first-in, first-out task queue locking concurrent generation to one task at a time to prevent CPU thrashing on CPU-only servers, returning a polite Tagalog busy notice if the queue limit is reached.
Two-Pass Generation & Grammar Refinement: Implemented primary Tagalog response generation followed by an automated grammar-correction second pass with a fallback mechanism that reverts to the initial response if the correction times out or encounters errors.
Server-Sent Events Streaming Support: Added real-time token streaming capability that automatically bypasses the secondary grammar pass to maintain sub-second response times.
FAQ Knowledge Base Embedding: Directly embedded all 20 verified ground-truth FAQ operational solutions into the system prompt, enforcing natural, grammatically correct Tagalog responses even when users prompt in English or Taglish.
Security & Operational Controls: Enforced header-based API key authentication, dual-layer rate limiting per IP address and session ID, a 120-second execution timeout, and sanitized logging to prevent message leakage in production.
Containerization & Deployment Configuration: Prepared multi-stage container build instructions, internal network configurations, memory limit boundaries, volume persistence rules, model pull commands, and verification benchmarks.
